Nov 8 : Mercedes completed a Formula One title double in Brazil on Sunday, adding the constructors' crown to Kimi Antonelli's drivers' championship won in Mexico City last weekend and celebrating with champagne and the whole race team dancing on the podium. While 20-year-old Italian Antonelli's success in becoming the youngest ever champion will have grabbed more headlines, the team title is nonetheless meaningful for what it brings in financial rewards and Mercedes have had four lean years since their last in 2021. The constructors' title is where the team gets its reward, a greater share of the sport's prize pot and prestige for sponsors, and is the trigger for staff bonuses that affect everyone working long days at the Brackley and Brixworth factories in England. "They're all different, with different challenges and situations," said team principal and co-owner Toto Wolff ahead of the race at Interlagos when asked about the many titles he has now presided over.

"The drivers' was very special this year, but the constructors' is obviously the one that pays the bonuses. So, it's something that is very, very important for all of the organisation. "You know - you pay the mortgage, the (new) kitchen, or the holiday, or the school of the children. And the driver is also very aware of that." Mercedes now have 652 points to Ferrari's 512, an insurmountable lead of 140 with only 129 still to be won.  FOUR DIFFICULT YEARS According to some estimates, McLaren received $175 million for winning the title last season. Mercedes last clinched the double in 2020, with 2021 their last constructors' title - the end of a record run of eight in a row - and have fought back from a difficult period with a bouncing car and wins in short supply. "We've had four pretty difficult years. To come back, it feels as nice as we all thought it would feel," said Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin.  "There's so many of the team members who have joined since we had the period ending in 2021, so they won't have experienced this."  Red Bull won in 2022 and 2023 and Mercedes-powered McLaren the next two, clinching their own double with Sunday's race winner Lando Norris last year. Mercedes have now equalled 1980s and 1990s champions Williams on nine constructors' titles, behind only Ferrari (16) and McLaren (10). The seeds of the 2026 championship success were sown early in the season, with Mercedes winning the first six races and Antonelli five in a row. STRONG START TO THE SEASON "It was a very strong beginning of the season and that kind of got us over the line. These last few races have been challenging at times, today it was difficult, but overall I'm so proud for the organisation," said Wolff on Sunday. "We have taken a few years to be back at the top spot. Not many teams have been able to come back from such a situation and it just shows the great work, the great people we have in our organisation and it's great to be among them."  Sunday could mark the start of a new streak of Mercedes domination, or be simply the reward for the team starting the sport's new engine rules era with the best overall package before others caught up. Red Bull, with their own in-house engine, won three of the four races before Brazil while second-placed Ferrari outscored Mercedes in the four races immediately leading up to Interlagos. The competition is out there and ready to step up next year.     "I don't think in this day and age, with the professionalism that teams have now, you can replicate what we did, eight championships in a row," said Wolff. "There's three or four teams that will be competing for a championship next year and it could go either way."

Source: Reuters

Nov 8 : Lazio's lead at the top of Serie A was cut to one point on Sunday after they were held to a 1-1 draw at Napoli, while Inter Milan beat Como 2-0 to close in on the unbeaten leaders. Davide Frattesi put Lazio ahead in the 28th minute, finishing off a counter-attack after being played in by Tijjani Noslin. Napoli equalised three minutes after halftime when Lazio substitute Alfonso Pedraza inadvertently deflected a cross into his own net. Lazio remain top with 29 points, one ahead of Inter and two clear of third-placed AS Roma. Napoli are 10th on 15 points after a sluggish start to the season. The draw provided only limited relief for Napoli after a run of poor results that included Wednesday's 4–1 Champions League defeat by Porto.

Manager Massimiliano Allegri has won only five of his opening 15 matches in charge, prompting sporting director Giovanni Manna to describe the situation as "unacceptable". Allegri urged calm despite the mounting pressure. "There are difficult moments over the course of a campaign," he told DAZN. "I believe we need to deal with them in a spirit of calm, try to recover those who are injured, and bring simplicity and organisation to the situation." While Napoli struggle, the capital's clubs are enjoying a record start. Roma and Lazio are the first teams from the same city to remain unbeaten after the opening 11 matches of a Serie A season, with Roma winning 3-0 against Sassuolo on Saturday. Despite leading the pack, Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso played down talk of a title challenge. "We don’t really belong up there, we have to take it day by day," Gattuso said. INTER CLOSE GAP Inter, looking to respond after dropping points in their previous league match, made an aggressive start against visitors Como, who were riding high after a stunning 9-1 Champions League victory at French side Lens on Wednesday. Francesco Pio Esposito prodded home from close range in the 12th minute before Marcus Thuram punished a poor clearance to double Inter's advantage seven minutes later. Como remained competitive but rarely threatened a comeback, while Inter went closer to adding a third than the visitors did to cutting the deficit. AC Milan won 2-1 at Genoa earlier on Sunday, with early goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic lifting them to 24 points, one ahead of Como.

Source: Reuters

CAIRO: Two passenger trains collided some 76 km south of Cairo on Sunday (Nov 8), killing at least seven people and injuring 112, Egypt ’s health ministry said. The state railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum hit the back of another heading from Cairo to Aswan, derailing several carriages. Emergency crews were clearing the wreckage to restore services on the Cairo-Upper Egypt line, the railway authority said, without giving any indication of how long this would take. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered a swift investigation and said anyone found negligent should be held accountable, according to a separate statement. Egypt 's public prosecutor's office said investigations were underway to determine the technical reasons behind the crash. Egypt has one of the oldest and largest railway networks in the region and accidents involving casualties are common, though t he government has been investing billions of Egypt ian pounds to modernise the network. In the country's worst-ever rail disaster, a fire tore through seven carriages of an overcrowded passenger service in 2002, killing at least 360 people.

MANCHESTER, England, Nov 8 : Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is facing another international window filled with uncertainty after his side slipped into the Premier League relegation zone despite a sensational comeback to claim a 4-4 home draw with Aston Villa.  United are 18th on eight points after 10 games, one behind Coventry City, and for long periods of Sunday's game looked like a disjointed, rudderless side, with collapses in concentration at the start of each half proving costly for Carrick's men.  Alysson opened the scoring for Villa after two minutes and Nicolas Jackson added a second two minutes later, but United looked to be motoring when Bruno Fernandes pulled one back with a penalty and Youri Tielemans levelled just before the break.  United again conceded twice in quick succession at the start of the second half to goals from John McGinn and Leon Goretzka but Joshua Zirkzee threw them a lifeline in stoppage time and Patrick Dorgu headed the equaliser in the 96th minute.

"I don't feel happy," Dorgu said, despite his late heroics. "We are in a bad situation. We need to fight together to get out of it. Draw better than a loss, but we had the better opportunities.  "Everyone needs to look at themselves and ask if they are doing enough. We need to fight for the manager, for the club and get out of this together ... we need everyone to come back sharp from the international break and start getting wins." After the final whistle, Carrick said he thought his side had done enough to win but individual errors had cost them.  "I thought we were the better team for a large part of the game. We're making it difficult for ourselves with the goals that we're giving away, and not just giving away one — it's kind of two in succession that put us in such a difficult position," he told Sky Sports. "Then (we) came back into the game and had a lot of the game, and then could have won it in the end, so disappointed that we haven't won again." United fans unfurled banners calling for a change of ownership and booed and whistled some players as they were replaced, but the supporters celebrated with abandon when their side snatched a point at the death. "They are desperate to get behind us and for us to give them something to go on, they've showed that there's frustration and disappointment at times, I think we all feel that, but they're right behind the boys," Carrick said.  "They were (there) right till the end today, and they were after the final whistle as well." Asked about his own future after another underwhelming display, Carrick remained tight-lipped.  "We haven't won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on things that we've been working on and showing a lot of the good (we showed) in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches," he said.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Nov 8 : Makeshift England winger Henry Pollock thinks playing in that position is easy after scoring two tries against Australia, his coach Steve Borthwick said on Sunday. Back-row forward Pollock, 21, replaced the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso at halftime in the Nations Championship game at Twickenham, dotting down quickfire tries in the hosts' record 45-22 win. "He is going round the changing room telling the wingers it is easy, so we have that to deal with," Borthwick told the BBC. "Henry is as quick as our wingers and arguably he would say he is more talented. We have been preparing that for over a year now and to play 40 minutes on the wing, he deserves enormous credit."

England secured only their fourth win in nine matches this year, easing the pressure on Borthwick with a vibrant offensive display, but the coach also praised his team's discipline. "We are in an era where attack is dominant and that defensive performance was really strong," he said. "There was only one line break and that was an intercepted pass. "The players have been brilliant in their preparation. Every minute mattered and they have been laser-focused on producing a performance out there." Australia coach Les Kiss was disconsolate after his team's fourth loss in 10 matches this year. "I am disappointed, there is frustration. They are training well and working hard but they are not transferring that into the minutes," Kiss said. "Credit to England, they kept us in our third in the first half and made their way into our tryline area. They were very good and clinical." Australia scored second-half consolation tries through replacement centre Filipo Daugunu and flanker Jeremy Williams to make the scoreline more respectable. "We went out with intention in the second half, we needed to be better but it was too little too late," Kiss said. "This wasn't a true reflection of us but that is what happened. We need to be better." The Wallabies struggled to contain the England pack and prop Angus Bell was sent to the sin bin for a dangerous tackle in the first half. "Losses like that make you sit back and make you take an internal look into a few things," Kiss said. "It is important to not look too far and too wide, we need to narrow down a few things that we can work on together. It is a disappointment tonight but we have seven days to turn that around." Australia play Scotland on Sunday lying third in the Nations Championship Southern Hemisphere standings behind South Africa and New Zealand. England are second in the Northern Hemisphere table, two points behind France ahead of their game against Japan on Saturday.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Colombia se compromete a proteger a los periodistas amenazados por las bandas de narcotraficantes
item.description: El presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, ordenó reforzar la seguridad de los medios de comunicación en este país andino, alegando alertas de los servicios de inteligencia sobre posibles ata ...
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, ordenó reforzar la seguridad de los medios de comunicación en el país andino, alegando alertas de los servicios de inteligencia sobre posibles ataques contra instalaciones de radiodifusión por parte de un importante grupo guerrillero. “La libertad de prensa es sagrada y debe respetarse”, afirmó De la Espriella el domingo en una publicación en X. “Ningún grupo narcoterrorista silenciará a los medios de comunicación mediante amenazas, intimidación o actos de violencia”. VER MÁS: Peña, de Paraguay, fue acusado de delitos tras ser destituido como presidente Se movilizarán los servicios de seguridad para proteger a las cadenas de televisión y radio RCN y Caracol, mientras que se reforzará la protección de la que ya goza la revista Semana. “Se movilizará toda la capacidad del Estado” para “proteger a estos medios de comunicación, a sus periodistas, a su personal y a sus familias”, afirmó el presidente. De la Espriella, un conservador de línea dura que llegó al poder este año, está actuando con firmeza contra los grupos armados ilegales como el ELN, al que mencionó en su declaración del domingo. La estrategia incluye la colaboración con la Administración del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump y supone una ruptura radical con la de su predecesor de izquierdas, quien intentó desarmar a las guerrillas dedicadas al tráfico de cocaína mediante la negociación. La violencia ha ido en aumento a medida que las fuerzas gubernamentales se enfrentan a los grupos armados. El sábado, un ataque con drones contra una base militar en el norte de Colombia causó la muerte de tres soldados, según informó el ejército en un comunicado emitido el domingo por la mañana. La zona es un centro neurálgico de la actividad minera ilegal de oro, cuyo control es objeto de disputa entre el ELN, el Clan del Golfo y otras facciones guerrilleras. “Cada ataque contra nuestros soldados refuerza nuestra determinación de defender a Colombia”, afirmó De La Espriella en respuesta al ataque con drones. FAST

SAO PAULO, Nov 8 : Mercedes secured their ninth Formula One constructors' world championship and completed a title double on Sunday in a Sao Paulo Grand Prix won by McLaren's Lando Norris from pole position for the second year in a row. The title was Mercedes' first constructors' crown since 2021 and came a week after 20-year-old Italian Kimi Antonelli became the youngest drivers' champion with four races to spare in Mexico City. Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished second, racing from 21st on the grid due to engine penalties, in a race that started and ended in the rain, and teammate Isack Hadjar was third. George Russell was fourth for Mercedes and Antonelli fifth with the fastest lap.  Mercedes had needed to score only three points more than Ferrari to clinch the title and the Italian team never threatened to prolong the fight on a treacherous track with Charles Leclerc seventh and Lewis Hamilton ninth in his 400th race.

"It was a very tough race, very, very tough," said Norris, the 2025 world champion, of his 14th career win and 50th podium as well as his team's first victory since August. "A lot of challenges today with the conditions and going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you are pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit," added the Briton, who lost out to Antonelli at the start. "The main thing today was I kept it cool and didn't make any mistakes and had the pace when I needed to. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well." Norris took the chequered flag, waved by Brazil soccer forward Neymar, 14.602 seconds clear of Verstappen.  Mercedes equalled Williams' nine constructors' championships. "It was a very strong beginning of the season and that kind of got us over the line. These last few races have been challenging at times, today it was difficult, but overall I'm so proud for the organisation," said team boss Toto Wolff. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was sixth with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson sandwiched between the Ferrari drivers in eighth after a fine race that saw the New Zealander start third and run in second place for the first five laps. Nico Hulkenberg took the final point for Audi in a race of spins, slippery moments and changeable conditions. (Writing by Alan Baldwin in London, editing by Toby Davis)

Source: Reuters

item.title: La Torre de Saudi Aramco, objetivo de un inusual ataque contra el centro financiero de Riad
item.description: Un ataque de los hutíes ha dañado uno de los edificios emblemáticos del distrito financiero de la capital de Arabia Saudí, lo que ha trastocado los planes de vuelta a la normalidad aproximadamente un ...
item.dc:creator: Christine Burke
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Un ataque de los hutíes ha dañado uno de los edificios emblemáticos del distrito financiero de la capital de Arabia Saudita, lo que ha trastocado los planes de vuelta a la normalidad aproximadamente un mes después de que unos ataques mortales contra el aeropuerto de Riad interrumpieran el tráfico aéreo y provocaran la cancelación de eventos emblemáticos. Las oficinas de la gigante petrolera estatal Saudi Aramco sufrieron daños leves mientras la ciudad se defendía el domingo de una nueva oleada de misiles balísticos y de crucero. No hubo fallecidos ni heridos, según informó la agencia estatal de noticias Saudi Press Agency. VER MÁS: Arabia Saudita busca reducir su dependencia del estrecho de Ormuz con más oleoductos Los hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán y que llevan una década en conflicto con Arabia Saudí, reivindicaron la autoría del ataque. Las autoridades saudíes afirmaron posteriormente que habían respondido destruyendo dos lanzamisiles utilizados en los intentos de ataque. Este inusual ataque contra el centro financiero de Riad, conocido como KAFD, no contribuirá a tranquilizar a las empresas internacionales, que ya se ven afectadas por meses de conflicto regional. El KAFD alberga el Fondo de Inversión Pública de Arabia Saudí, así como la bolsa de valores, consultoras internacionales y gigantes financieros como Goldman Sachs y Brookfield. El incidente se produjo mientras en el KAFD se aplicaban medidas de teletrabajo —lo que limitó las repercusiones inmediatas—, pero tuvo lugar durante la hora punta de la mañana y justo cuando muchos colegios de Riad reanudaban las clases presenciales por primera vez en un mes. La KAFD comunicó a los inquilinos hace unos días que podían volver a las oficinas, pero el sábado se echó atrás y ordenó volver al teletrabajo hasta nuevo aviso. Los últimos ataques podrían provocar nuevas restricciones de viaje para los ejecutivos que viajan constantemente entre Riad y centros como Dubái, Abu Dabi y Londres. Se produjeron casi un mes después de que los ataques hutíes contra el principal aeropuerto de Riad causaran la muerte de más de una docena de personas y dejaran cientos de heridos. Esta agitación amenaza con ejercer una presión aún mayor sobre el príncipe heredero y líder de facto de Arabia Saudí, Mohammed bin Salman, en un momento en que se esfuerza por mantener en marcha su plan de diversificación económica de varios billones de dólares. Durante el último mes, el reino se ha visto obligado a aplazar o cancelar eventos —entre ellos la Copa Asiática de la AFC y el foro de la FII— que prometían ser un gran impulso para la economía y para el esfuerzo general por atraer más inversión extranjera. Arabia Saudí se enfrenta a un déficit presupuestario creciente, al tiempo que su economía se contrae y el mercado bursátil muestra un comportamiento anémico. El tráfico aéreo en el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid de Riad sigue siendo limitado, ya que muchas aerolíneas internacionales siguen restringiendo los viajes. La KAFD no respondió el domingo a una solicitud de comentarios. A principios del fin de semana, los hutíes amenazaron con atacar infraestructuras saudíes en respuesta a los ataques de las fuerzas lideradas por Arabia Saudí en Yemen. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán condenó el domingo lo que calificó de ataques aéreos saudíes contra infraestructuras civiles en Yemen e instó a que cesaran de inmediato los ataques. Asimismo, abogó por que el conflicto entre Arabia Saudí y Yemen se resolviera mediante el diálogo. La escalada entre Arabia Saudí y los hutíes se produce en un momento en que aumentan las especulaciones en Oriente Medio sobre los próximos acontecimientos en la guerra entre EE. UU. e Irán y las elecciones en Israel. VER MÁS: Aramco alerta que el colchón mundial de petróleo es preocupantemente bajo por la crisis de Ormuz Según ha informado Bloomberg, Washington y Teherán se están acercando a un posible avance en los esfuerzos por poner fin al conflicto tras un estancamiento que se ha prolongado durante meses. En Israel, el candidato electoral Gadi Eisenkot ha dado un paso más hacia el fin del mandato del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu tras obtener la oportunidad de formar un nuevo Gobierno. Aramco se ha convertido en un objetivo semirregular de los ataques desde que EE. UU. e Israel entraron en guerra con Irán a finales de febrero. Sin embargo, la frecuencia de los ataques se ha acelerado en los últimos meses, al intensificar los hutíes sus intentos de asalto contra el transporte marítimo y las infraestructuras saudíes. Entre los activos que se han visto amenazados se encuentran la sede central de Aramco en Dhahran, su principal centro petrolero en Ras Tanura, en el Golfo Pérsico, y el oleoducto Este-Oeste que transporta crudo hasta el mar Rojo para su exportación. Aramco ha declarado que pretende ampliar la capacidad de sus oleoductos y almacenar más petróleo en el extranjero, con el objetivo de aumentar su resiliencia y protegerse frente a posibles interrupciones. item.title: Gross plays down Brighton's title credentials despite move to second

Gross plays down Brighton's title credentials despite move to second

BRIGHTON, Nov 8 : Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Pascal Gross dismissed his side's Premier League title credentials on Sunday despite a 2-0 home victory over Brentford that lifted the south coast club to second in the table. Fabian Huerzeler's impressive side have 22 points from 10 games and head into the international break as champions Arsenal's closest pursuers, five points adrift. The club's best-ever start to a top-flight season included a 3-0 home win over Arsenal and has left the fans dreaming of an unlikely title challenge, less than 10 years after they were promoted from the second tier. But Gross, who scored Brighton's second goal from the penalty spot after a spectacular opener by Diego Gomez, is keeping his feet firmly on the ground.

"No. We are not in a title race. But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season," the German said. "You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet. "Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this." Whatever Gross thinks, the statistics make a strong case. Brighton, whose best finish was sixth in 2022-23 under Roberto de Zerbi, are clearly not second by accident. No team has scored more than their 26 goals in the top flight this season and only Arsenal have conceded fewer. Brighton are competing in the UEFA Conference League following their eighth place finish last season and Huerzeler is balancing the demands of the hectic schedule. After last week's victory at Manchester City they travelled to Spain to beat Getafe in midweek but looked fresh against Brentford, albeit helped by the visitors being reduced to 10 men after Igor Thiago was sent off in the first half. Huerzeler, who became the Premier League's youngest permanent manager when he joined Brighton, aged 31, in 2024 said the fans are entitled to dream. "They should always be excited if they watch our game, and that's our job to make them excited," he said. "And I always say they can dream, they can have high expectations of us, but these are things we can't control." With fixtures against the likes of Hull City, Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest after the international break, Brighton could maintain their position near the top. Huerzeler said his side still had room to can improve. "There are moments and phases in the game where the individual player, but also the whole team, can improve, and that's the main focus for us," he said. "It was from the beginning, and it will be also now, and it will be also in the rest of the season."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Subaru y Toyota han eligieron el momento perfecto para lanzar al mercado vehículos eléctricos asequibles
item.description: Los fabricantes de automóviles han más que duplicado sus ventas de vehículos eléctricos en Estados Unidos en lo que va de año, ya que los conductores buscan formas de ahorrar en gasolina.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Stock
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Karla Fisher, marine e ingeniera jubilada, podría decirse que debería haberse comprado un vehículo eléctrico hace un año. Existían incentivos federales y una gran variedad de opciones, entre las que se incluían la Ford F-150 Lightning, la Honda Prologue y la Nissan Ariya, todas ellas desaparecidas desde entonces. Sin embargo, ninguno de esos vehículos cumplía del todo con los requisitos específicos de la Sra. Fisher: una distancia al suelo de al menos siete pulgadas, una autonomía superior a las 250 millas y un precio en línea con —o ligeramente inferior- al de las alternativas de gasolina. VER MÁS: Los clubes de lujo compiten por satisfacer a los padres con una demanda desbordante El Subaru Trailseeker, un nuevo modelo que salió al mercado a principios de este año, cumplía todos esos requisitos. La Sra. Fisher compró el suyo en septiembre y ya ha recorrido 2.000 millas con él, conduciendo hasta puntos de partida de rutas de senderismo, lugares de pesca y campings cercanos a su hogar en la costa de Oregón. “Llevo más de una década siguiendo de cerca el mercado de los vehículos eléctricos”, afirmó. “Por desgracia, en todo ese tiempo no se fabricó ningún coche que me pareciera una opción sensata como consumidora”. El Subaru eléctrico, afirma, es ahora su “coche favorito de todos los tiempos”. Mientras los directivos del sector automovilístico estadounidense se mostraban cada vez más reticentes respecto a los coches eléctricos este año, retirando modelos y recortando la producción, Subaru Corp. y Toyota Motor Corp. se colaron en ese vacío. Con cinco nuevos modelos, ambas empresas han vendido conjuntamente casi 62 000 vehículos eléctricos en EE. UU. durante los tres primeros trimestres de 2026, más del doble de la cifra registrada el año anterior. Aunque estas marcas siguen representando solo el 9% del mercado estadounidense de vehículos eléctricos y se sitúan por detrás de General Motors Co. en este segmento, sus ventas están creciendo, mientras que las de sus rivales han experimentado un retroceso. En lo que va de año, Rivian Automotive Inc., que también ha incorporado una nueva camioneta a su gama, es el único otro fabricante de automóviles que ha registrado un aumento en su negocio de vehículos eléctricos. Subaru y Toyota se han incorporado relativamente tarde a la carrera de los coches eléctricos, pero el momento les es propicio. Si bien la demanda de vehículos eléctricos se enfrió cuando expiraron los incentivos federales en septiembre, el mercado se ha estabilizado y el número de conductores interesados en los vehículos eléctricos va en aumento. Los analistas señalan que ambas marcas están captando a conductores desconcertados por los elevados precios de la gasolina y una cuota de mercado que, de otro modo, podría haber ido a parar a manos de rivales más grandes que han descartado los modelos eléctricos. “Se trata de un reinicio para el mercado de los vehículos eléctricos y es una muestra de resiliencia”, afirmó Stephanie Valdez Streaty, directora de análisis del sector en Cox Automotive Inc. “Y se empieza a observar esta divergencia entre quienes están ganando la carrera y quienes se están retirando”. Toyota, propietaria del 20% de Subaru, vende actualmente en EE. UU. dos vehículos eléctricos por cada uno de los que vende Ford. Y aunque Subaru sigue siendo un actor de menor envergadura, Valdez Streaty señaló que está sacando partido del resurgimiento del interés por los vehículos eléctricos. Los nuevos vehículos eléctricos de estas empresas son SUV asequibles, que constituyen el segmento estrella del mercado automovilístico estadounidense, añadió. En cierta medida, el auge de las ventas requirió tanta suerte como estrategia. Si bien lleva mucho tiempo llevar un nuevo modelo de coche desde el boceto hasta la cadena de montaje, descartarlo es relativamente rápido. Cuando el mercado estadounidense de vehículos eléctricos se desplomó a finales del año pasado, se retiraron de la producción varios modelos en cuestión de semanas. Mientras tanto, los nuevos vehículos eléctricos de Subaru y Toyota llevaban años en desarrollo y casualmente debutaron justo cuando los precios de la gasolina se dispararon y la oferta de vehículos eléctricos se había reducido considerablemente. “Ha habido tanta volatilidad en el sector de los vehículos eléctricos en lo que respecta a la normativa que ha sido una experiencia interesante”, afirmó Timothy Tagye, vicepresidente de operaciones de campo de Subaru of America Inc. “Pero nuestro momento fue el adecuado”. Un aspecto fundamental es que las empresas se han asociado para desarrollar muchos de sus últimos vehículos eléctricos, compartiendo recursos y repartiendo los costes. Aunque cada marca ha imprimido su sello distintivo en el diseño exterior, bajo la carrocería, gran parte de la mecánica es común. El portavoz de Subaru, Dominick Infante, señaló que este acuerdo es la razón principal por la que los precios de venta de los vehículos —entre los que se incluyen el Trailseeker y el Uncharted de Subaru, y el C-HR y el bZ Woodland de Toyota— son relativamente asequibles. Con precios que oscilan entre los 35000 y los 45000 dólares, todos los nuevos modelos se sitúan muy por debajo del precio medio de venta de un coche de combustión interna en Estados Unidos en la actualidad. “Creemos firmemente que el futuro está en los vehículos eléctricos”, afirmó Infante. Toyota señaló que, desde hace tiempo, su estrategia ha consistido en evitar intentar discernir si la industria del automóvil se decantaría por los vehículos de gasolina o por los eléctricos. Sus nuevos vehículos eléctricos no son más que otra opción, junto a los híbridos y los vehículos que funcionan exclusivamente con gasolina, según Owen Peacock, director general de marketing y comunicaciones de Toyota. VER MÁS: Papamóvil de Toyota: cómo es la Hilux que usará el papa León XIV en Argentina Ambas marcas se encuentran ahora en una situación ideal en lo que respecta a los vehículos eléctricos en EE. UU.: SUV de tamaño pequeño, mediano y grande. El año que viene, cada una de ellas añadirá un modelo extragrande a su gama. Se espera que en primavera llegue una versión eléctrica del SUV Toyota Highlander de tres filas de asientos, que Subaru comercializará como un nuevo modelo denominado Getaway. «Nuestra estrategia de múltiples vías se basa, en realidad, en el principio de “satisfacer las necesidades de todo el mundo”», afirmó Peacock, «en lugar de “llevar a la gente de una opción a otra y de otra a otra”». item.title: Wall Street se lanza a la carrera por las megatransacciones mientras comienza la cuenta regresiva para la era Trump
item.description: El regreso del presidente Donald Trump a la Casa Blanca ha cambiado el panorama político en torno a las fusiones y adquisiciones, reavivando el interés de las empresas por operaciones de ensueño que s ...
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El regreso del presidente Donald Trump a la Casa Blanca ha cambiado los cálculos políticos en torno a las fusiones y adquisiciones, reavivando el deseo de las empresas de cerrar acuerdos soñados que se habían vuelto difíciles de llevar a cabo. Ahora, el mundo empresarial estadounidense se encuentra contra reloj. La derrota sufrida por los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura está generando una repentina sensación de urgencia en las salas de juntas, donde los ejecutivos se preguntan si podrían tener una última oportunidad de llevar a cabo una operación transformadora mientras los reguladores favorables a las fusiones y adquisiciones sigan en sus puestos bajo el mandato de Trump. VER MÁS: Agenda de la semana: inflación en EE.UU. y Brasil, tasas en Perú y la COPt31 Las conversaciones con los principales asesores sugieren que el resultado ya está llevando a las empresas a preguntarse si deberían actuar con rapidez para llevar adelante grandes movimientos estratégicos. Existe la conciencia de que un Partido Demócrata resurgente podría intentar frustrar el tipo de acuerdos espectaculares que han cobrado impulso durante la “era Trump 2.0″ y que han impulsado unos ingresos récord en Wall Street. Kevin Foley, codirector de banca de inversión de JPMorgan Chase & Co., una de las principales firmas de asesoramiento del mundo, afirmó que las empresas deberían estar preparadas para realizar operaciones en otro entorno operativo complicado. “El mayor riesgo puede ser dar por sentado que, tarde o temprano, las cosas volverán a la normalidad”, señaló Foley, con sede en Nueva York. “Quedarse quieto siempre es una opción, pero cuando los sectores están cambiando a este ritmo, es la opción equivocada”. Fernando Rivas, un alto directivo de Wells Fargo & Co., lo expresó de forma más contundente en una conferencia del sector celebrada el jueves en Boston, al afirmar que la mentalidad de “ahora o nunca” volverá a impulsar las fusiones y adquisiciones a corto plazo. Los dos mandatos de Trump han supuesto una proporción desmesurada de las operaciones más importantes. Más de la mitad de todas las transacciones anunciadas con un valor de al menos US$50.000 millones y en las que ha participado una empresa estadounidense durante las últimas dos décadas se han producido mientras él era presidente, según un análisis de datos recopilados por Bloomberg. Solo este año se han producido fusiones históricas en sectores de importancia crítica como la energía y la tecnología, como la adquisición récord de este mes, por más de US$100.000 millones, del fabricante de láseres Lumentum Holdings Inc. por parte de Marvell Technology Inc. Por otra parte, el Departamento de Justicia autorizó la adquisición de Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. por parte de Paramount Skydance Corp., por valor de US$110.000 millones de dólares, sin imponer medidas correctoras en materia de competencia. VER MÁS: Los temores inflacionarios resurgen y las empresas estadounidenses calculan el impacto en sus costos Existe una urgencia especial por poner en marcha estas transacciones más complejas. Las megatransacciones pueden tardar meses en negociarse y aún más en superar los controles regulatorios en todo el mundo. Las empresas que esperen hasta que la campaña presidencial de 2028 esté en pleno apogeo para seguir adelante con este tipo de acuerdos corren el riesgo de que se conviertan en tema de debate político durante la campaña electoral. “Si se tiene una operación de gran envergadura que va a llevar tiempo preparar y tramitar, realmente hay que empezar a trabajar en ella ahora mismo y, probablemente, anunciarla a mediados de 2027″, afirmó Paul Nary, profesor adjunto de gestión en la Wharton School de la Universidad de Pensilvania. “No queda mucho tiempo”. Un caso de prueba clave para las megafusiones y adquisiciones en el nuevo panorama podría ser la posible unión de SpaceX y Tesla Inc., de Elon Musk, que se contaría entre las fusiones empresariales más grandes y políticamente delicadas jamás intentadas y revelaría el alcance de la influencia del multimillonario sobre Trump, a medida que el equilibrio de poder en Washington comienza a cambiar. Bloomberg News ha informado que Musk, quien destinó casi US$500 millones a apoyar a candidatos republicanos en elecciones clave de mitad de legislatura, está presionando para anunciar una fusión de sus dos mayores empresas antes del primer semestre de 2027. Sin embargo, la situación se ha complicado; las acciones tanto de SpaceX como de Tesla se han desplomado ante el temor de que un Congreso liderado por los demócratas investigue los negocios y las relaciones políticas de Musk y, en términos más generales, intente frenar el auge de la inteligencia artificial que él ha defendido constantemente. VER MÁS: Tesla y SpaceX caen en picada tras la derrota electoral de Trump y el avance demócrata en EE.UU. Aunque los demócratas no asumirán el control del Departamento de Justicia ni de la Comisión Federal de Comercio —lo que mantendrá en sus puestos a los responsables de la aplicación de la normativa sobre fusiones del Gobierno—, hacerse con el control de ambas cámaras proporcionará al partido nuevas vías para examinar fusiones y adquisiciones de gran envergadura y carácter sensible mediante audiencias, investigaciones y citaciones judiciales, además de avivar el escrutinio público sobre las empresas y los organismos reguladores. Varias operaciones de gran envergadura que se encuentran en trámite, e incluso algunas que ya se han completado, podrían convertirse en los primeros objetivos del Congreso renovado a partir de enero. La adquisición por parte de DoorDash Inc. de Maplebear Inc., empresa matriz de Instacart, por valor de U$S17.000 millones, ha suscitado críticas de destacados demócratas, entre ellos el alcalde de la ciudad de Nueva York, Zohran Mamdani, quien afirmó que la operación supondría “precios más altos, una explotación más severa y una mayor desigualdad económica”. Por su parte, legisladores como los senadores Ed Markey y Richard Blumenthal han puesto en el punto de mira la compra de Dominion Energy Inc. por parte de NextEra Energy Inc., por valor de US$67.000 millones , advirtiendo de que podría reducir la competencia y elevar los costes para los consumidores. Y el senador Cory Booker se ha comprometido a que el Congreso supervise minuciosamente la operación entre Paramount y Warner Bros., que se cerró el mes pasado. “El Congreso dispone de tiempo y recursos limitados, por lo que no va a investigar todas las transacciones”, afirmó Paul Humphreys, codirector global del departamento de industria del bufete de abogados Freshfields. “Es de esperar que la atención se centre en temas concretos, especialmente la asequibilidad y la rendición de cuentas”. “El Congreso tiene la capacidad de citar a ejecutivos, emitir citaciones y situar una operación en el punto de mira político, incluso después de que haya sido autorizada”, señaló Humphreys. El declive del sector de la IA plantea un reto más inmediato para los negociadores que han aprovechado el desarrollo de esta tecnología para impulsar algunas de las operaciones más importantes del segundo mandato de Trump. Los centros de datos fueron tema de debate en múltiples estados durante las elecciones de mitad de legislatura, y los votantes acabaron dando un rotundo revés a su rápida expansión por todo Estados Unidos. Los mercados, que ya venían lidiando con la inquietud generada por el enorme gasto de capital en torno a la IA, ahora también están teniendo en cuenta la posibilidad de que se impongan restricciones más estrictas a la infraestructura digital que la sustenta. El índice de semiconductores de la Bolsa de Filadelfia —un barómetro para las empresas de chips— sufrió la semana pasada su mayor caída en un solo día desde que estalló la pandemia de la COVID-19 en marzo de 2020. Esta caída ha puesto de relieve la operación entre Marvell y Lumentum. Ambas empresas han registrado fuertes caídas desde las elecciones de mitad de legislatura, lo que añade otra variable a una transacción íntegramente en acciones cuya justificación estratégica se basa en gran medida en la inversión continuada en centros de datos y conectividad para la IA. Algunas firmas de Wall Street ampliaron su plantilla de empleados con contactos políticos, apostando por que un mejor acceso a la Administración Trump —y una mejor comprensión de la misma— sería crucial para sacar adelante grandes operaciones. Los resultados de las elecciones de mitad de legislatura podrían dar un vuelco a esa situación y obligar a los bancos a empezar a tender puentes con los demócratas antes de lo esperado. “Los negociadores habían empezado a comprender cómo desenvolverse en la Casa Blanca de Trump y su enfoque respecto a las fusiones y adquisiciones», afirmó Nary, de la Wharton School. «Tras la ola azul, ahora también van a necesitar una estrategia para el Congreso". LONDON, Nov 8 : Henry Pollock scored two tries off the wing as fired-up England secured a record 45-22 bonus-point victory over Australia in the Nations Championship at Twickenham on Sunday. England's fourth win in nine matches this year was a welcome boost for coach Steve Borthwick after a dismal Six Nations campaign. It was also their 12th triumph over the Wallabies in their last 14 meetings. "I am really happy. We have only come together in the last week and prep time has been short but we have put on a great performance," England centre and man of the match Henry Slade told ITV. "It is nice for us to get some points on the board and to do it so early on in the competition is really pleasing."

England started fast and winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso finished a slick passing move to touch down after 90 seconds but the try was chalked off for a forward pass. Hooker Jamie George finished off a driving maul to score his 18th international try and, after Australia scrumhalf Ryan Lonergan kicked a penalty, Feyi-Waboso's powerful surge broke open the defence and flanker Ollie Chessum crashed over in the corner. Australia prop Angus Bell was shown a yellow card for a hip-drop tackle, and England took full advantage with another powerful forward drive from a lineout with prop Joe Heyes barrelling over the line. England sensed a fourth try but a loose pass from scrumhalf Jack van Poortvliet was intercepted by Australia winger Max Jorgensen, who sprinted over from long range and Lonergan's conversion cut the hosts' lead to 19-10 at the interval. POLLOCK QUICKFIRE DOUBLE Back-row forward Pollock, replacing the injured Feyi-Waboso on the wing, made ground down the left with his first touch and another swift passing movement set Tommy Freeman clear on the right, his inside pass finding Van Poortvliet who touched down. England continued to monopolise the ball and, with the Wallabies tiring, another siege on their tryline ended with the ball in Pollock's hands and he gleefully went over before indulging in his trademark celebration to the crowd. Two minutes later the blonde forward finished off another flowing move down the right to claim his eighth international try and extend England's lead to 38-10. Australia regrouped and grabbed two consolation tries when replacement centre Filipo Daugunu darted over in the left corner and flanker Jeremy Williams took advantage of a lineout error to score. England, however, had the last word, replacement scrumhalf Ben Spencer adding their seventh try from an interception to rack up their highest score against the Wallabies. Australia suffered their fourth defeat in 10 matches this year. "We started the game and we didn't get much ball and didn't get many A-zone entries," Australia captain Harry Wilson said. "England were the better team today. They fronted up physically and put us under the pump. Our defence was not physical enough." England play Japan on Saturday and Australia face Scotland on Sunday.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Nov 8 : Liverpool ended a two-match losing run in all competitions with a 3-1 win at Crystal Palace on Sunday, piling more pressure on home manager Pierre Sage whose side slumped to a fourth straight Premier League defeat and fell to the bottom of the table. Alexis Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead in the 40th minute, fellow midfielder Florian Wirtz doubled their advantage nine minutes after the restart and striker Alexander Isak sealed the win with an 89th-minute strike. Palace pulled a goal back deep into stoppage time when Eddie Nketiah converted a contentious penalty awarded after Liverpool left back Milos Kerkez and Palace forward Dario Osorio jumped for a header. "I am very upset because the ones in our box they are calling penalties and in the other box they are not. I know we are 3-0 and it's the 95th minute but I'm very upset ...," Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola told Sky Sports.

"It's a clash of heads. You can say it's 3-0 but, for me, there is more because it is not the first time this season and you compare ... I'm really upset. "The VAR took a lot of time. When you call a penalty and they are two minutes. Two repetitions, three repetitions, they are finding a way not to be called by the VAR. A clean sheet is not cheap in the Premier League and we wanted to win 3-0. "It is not just because of this penalty, it's because of a lot of things." Liverpool arrived at Selhurst Park in need of a response after a 1-0 home league defeat by champions Arsenal last weekend and a 3-2 Champions League loss at Fenerbahce on Wednesday. The win lifted Liverpool to fourth in the standings with 18 points from 10 matches, while Palace fell to 20th on seven points, with pressure continuing to mount on Sage. The 47-year-old Frenchman joined Palace on a three-year contract in June. Sage arrived in south London with an impressive pedigree, having been named Ligue 1 Manager of the Year after guiding Lens to a second-place finish and their first Coupe de France trophy. However, he has struggled to reproduce that success at Palace. "It's not good to go into the international break in this situation, two weeks without games ...," Sage told the BBC. "What we have to change (is) to be more efficient in how we defend and attack. We have to be more competitive. "At the moment, we create some things, we expect a lot of things but we don't have the results expected."

Source: Reuters

LUSAIL, Qatar, Nov 8 : Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi led from start to finish to win the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday, denying Marc Marquez a chance to seal the MotoGP title under the lights at the Lusail International Circuit after the Ducati rider finished second. Marquez needed to win the race while Jorge Martin had to finish outside the points to seal an eighth premier-class title but his Aprilia rival finished seventh, taking the championship fight to the penultimate round of the season in Portugal. Marquez has a 60-point lead over Martin ahead of the next Grand Prix in Portimao while Bezzecchi, who crashed out of Saturday's sprint in a duel with Marquez before making amends in the race, is 74 points behind. "It feels amazing. I'm very happy. It was the performance we deserve," said Bezzecchi, who became the first rider to win 12 races at 12 different circuits.

"It's been a fantastic weekend for us. I've been super quick and super comfortable on the bike. A shame about yesterday but it's part of the game. To bounce back like this makes everything even better." Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez finished third while his team mate Ai Ogura was fourth. KTM's Pedro Acosta was in contention for a podium early in the race but tyre pressure problems forced him to drop back and he finished sixth. BEZZECCHI SHUTS DOOR ON MARQUEZ Aprilia's polesitter Bezzecchi had the perfect start off the line and the Italian shut the door when Marquez attempted to overtake on the inside of turn one, where they had collided in Saturday's sprint. Marquez then found himself fighting Aprilia bikes all around him as Trackhouse rider Fernandez moved past him to drop the reigning champion down to third. Bezzecchi and Fernandez were soon more than a second clear of Marquez by lap two as the Ducati rider decided not to take any risks early on, with title rival Martin down in ninth place. But as the gap between the top two and Marquez steadily increased, an impatient Acosta overtook his future Ducati teammate to move up to third. However, Acosta was clearly struggling with tyre pressure, turning back and signalling Marquez to move back to third so he could slot in behind his compatriot and take advantage of the Ducati's slipstream. Although Martin managed to move up to fifth, little changed in the top six positions but Marquez suddenly picked up the pace on lap 13 by setting the race lap record at Lusail as he set his sights on Fernandez. With three laps to go, Marquez made his move and surged past the Trackhouse rider on the main straight, earning a roar of approval from the stands. But it was too late to launch an attack on Bezzecchi, who was more than three seconds ahead and took the chequered flag. "I was very clever about my strategy. I was just trying to manage the race in the first five laps, it didn't matter if Bezzecchi got away," Marquez said. "My race was with Martin especially. But then Acosta let me pass because he had a tyre pressure problem. "I tried to control my pace. I saw that in one part of the race I was super fast... Third position was okay, but I saw that Fernandez was struggling. So you never know, I attacked and (I have) four points more."

Source: Reuters

Nov 8 : Alessia Russo struck twice to give Arsenal a 2-1 victory at Liverpool that keeps them in touch with the chasing pack in the Women's Super League, while London City Lionesses stayed in the hunt with a 4-1 home win over Birmingham City on Sunday.  Four defeats in their opening eight games had left Arsenal trailing in the chase for Europe but Russo's goals either side of Beata Olsson's equaliser claimed the win that leaves them sixth on 13 points, six off third-placed London City.  "Towards the end, we defended for our lives and played with so much passion and pride for the shirt, we threw bodies in front of the goal," Arsenal boss Renee Slegers said. "We got it over the line with character and fight, really proud of that." With Chelsea held 1-1 by Everton on Saturday and Manchester City thrashing West Ham United 5-0 to move top on 25 points, the Lionesses had no room to slip-up and they raced into a 2-0 lead thanks to goals from Poppy Pattinson and Delphine Cascarino.

Nov 8 : Manchester United head into the international break in the Premier League relegation zone but with some hope and pride restored after scoring twice in stoppage time to rescue a chaotic 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa on Sunday. Brighton & Hove Albion had earlier risen to second place in the Premier League standings with a 2-0 home victory over Brentford but it was another Old Trafford rollercoaster that ended as the big talking point of the weekend's action. Under-pressure manager Michael Carrick, whose standing amongst the United faithful remains high despite a calamitous season so far, earned a boost in midweek as his side hit back from two goals down to beat AS Roma 3-2 in the Champions League. Another rescue act looked beyond his team though as Villa, who scored twice inside the opening five minutes through Alysson and Nicolas Jackson before a Bruno Fernandes penalty and an equaliser from Youri Tielemans, reasserted their dominance.

United crumbled early in the second half with Diogo Dalot conceding a needless spot kick for a foul on Alysson and John McGinn firing home the 48th-minute penalty. Leon Goretzka then restored Villa's two-goal lead five minutes later with a tap-in after sloppy United defending. But whatever the ills that have befallen the 20-times English champions, there is no denying their fighting spirit. Joshua Zirkzee gave United late hope by slotting home in stoppage time before substitute Patrick Dorgu headed in after Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki flapped at a corner - sparking delirium amongst the home fans. The unlikely draw left United in 18th place with a mere eight points from 10 games, above Sunderland only on goal difference after the Black Cats claimed a first league win since August by beating Chelsea 1-0 at the Stadium of Light. "I thought we were the better team," said Carrick. "We played some very good football and got back into the game. "Two goals again put us on the back foot. In the end, we could have even won it," added the United boss, who went through every imaginable emotion on the touchline. "We never gave up and never stopped believing." Crystal Palace slumped to the bottom after a 3-1 home defeat by Liverpool, who moved up to fourth. BRIGHTON'S LOFTY POSITION Fabian Huerzeler's Brighton are continuing to provide ample evidence to suggest their lofty position is not a false one and, while they were helped by Igor Thiago's red card midway through the first half, they beat Brentford at a canter. The 33-year-old German has led the club to their best-ever start to a top-flight season and they head into the international break on 22 points, with Arsenal on 27 after their 1-0 win at home to Hull City on Saturday. Brighton went ahead in the 15th minute when Diego Gomez, scorer of a wonder goal against Palace a few weeks ago, seized on a clearance at the edge of the area and struck a superb left-foot shot on the turn into the top corner. Brentford striker Thiago then got involved in a tussle with Chema Andres and after a VAR check the Brazilian was sent off. The hosts doubled their lead in the 42nd minute when Pascal Gross dispatched a penalty high into the net after Keane Lewis-Potter had held Luka Vuskovic. Despite the wave of euphoria on the south coast, Gross was quick to play down Brighton's title prospects. "No. We are not in a title race. But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season," the German said. "You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet. "Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this." LIVERPOOL BOUNCE BACK Liverpool bounced back from last week's defeat at home by Arsenal with Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak all on target at Selhurst Park. Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage time consolation penalty for Palace but the pressure is mounting on their French manager Pierre Sage and will only intensify with Palace rock bottom for the first time in almost nine years. "Today my job is not the most important thing. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and club," Sage said. Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris will be breathing a little easier though after his side upset Chelsea. Enzo Le Fee struck the only goal from the penalty spot in the 36th minute after Chelsea defender Levi Colwill was adjudged to have pulled Brian Brobbey to the ground. Bournemouth's fourth successive league win moved them up to seventh with Evanilson scoring for the fifth Premier League game in succession in a 2-1 victory at Ipswich Town.

Source: Reuters

PARIS, Nov 8 : Carlos Alcaraz avenged his loss to Ben Shelton in the US Open last eight as he edged the American 7-6(5) 7-5 to win the Paris Masters on Sunday, clinching his ninth ATP 1000 title. World number three Alcaraz controlled the contest from the baseline to become the first Spaniard to win the tournament since David Ferrer in 2012, while Shelton was left frustrated by an erratic forehand. "Today, it was one of the toughest challenges we have in tennis right now, facing Ben Shelton," said Alcaraz, whose US Open title defence was derailed by eventual finalist Shelton in a four-and-a-half-hour thriller in September. "He is doing better and better with every tournament so it's going to be even tougher facing him. So I'm just really happy that I found the way."

The first set remained deadlocked until the tiebreak, where US Open finalist Shelton overshot the baseline three times on his forehand, allowing the Spaniard to take the set. World number four Shelton capitalised on two double faults and wayward topspins from Alcaraz to go 3-2 up in the second, and extended the lead with two aces in the following game. But Alcaraz fought back with a break of his own to make it 4-4, landing two cross-court winners as Shelton netted a forehand and went long with another. With Alcaraz leading 6-5, Shelton stumbled again while serving to stay in the match, overshooting two forehands before the seven-times Grand Slam winner clinched victory with a perfectly timed backhand down the line. "It's something I've been chasing for a long time," Alcaraz said after finally winning the Paris Masters on his sixth attempt. The Australian Open champion has now won three titles since the heartbreak at Flushing Meadows as he looks to end the year on a bright note at the ATP Finals starting next Sunday, followed by the Davis Cup finals later this month.

Source: Reuters

item.title: AI selloff rejuvenates Asia's forgotten investment trades
item.description: Retreat from AI-linked stocks prompts investors to look towards undervalued markets such as India and China, while easing inflation and trade tensions add to their appeal ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: The unravelling of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asiaplaybook, reviving demand for out-of-favour Chinese and Indian stocks, and companies poised to benefit from easinginflation and trade tensions. Aberdeen Investments favours markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms.  Asia has been among the hardest hit by the market fallout from the Democrats’ sweep of US Congress. Many of the region’s biggest stocks are critical suppliers to the global AI buildout, leaving local markets exposed as investors brace forgreater scrutiny of the industry. “I expect investors to diversify more broadly and reduce their concentration in the AI trade,” said Rajeev De Mello, global macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management SA. “This should be supportive of China and other markets where valuations areless demanding,” he said. India’s appeal has grown as oil prices fell on expectations of an earlier end to the Iran war. Its lack of AI exposure is also now seen as an advantage. LOGOS Asset Management’s Charlie Hong said he sold his shares in SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, Intel and Lumentum Holdings last month and has since boosted his Indian holdings. India’s benchmark Nifty 50 gained 8.6 per cent last week, registering its best week since 2021, as overseas investors returned in force.

Nov 8 : South Africa have called up experienced lock Eben Etzebeth ahead of their Nations Championship fixtures against France and Ireland as uncapped flyhalf Yaqeen Ahmed returns home with a shoulder injury. • Etzebeth, 35, was initially ruled out of the November internationals through injury but has been called on after fellow second row Salmaan Moerat pulled out of the 66-7 victory over Italy on Saturday after suffering back spasms in the warm-up • Etzebeth is the most-capped Springbok with 147 test appearances and could be drafted straight into the matchday 23 against France when coach Rassie Erasmus names his team on Monday • Ahmed, 20, is one of six uncapped players in the squad but with enough cover at flyhalf, there will be no like-for-like replacement • “We opted to call up Eben, who will not only bring vast experience to the group at this vital stage of the Nations Championship, but also valuable leadership skills, especially with two important matches against France and Ireland,” Erasmus said in a statement on Sunday

Nov 8 : BC Partners has revived efforts to create a successor to LIV Golf, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, after the breakaway circuit said it would wind down operations following the collapse of a proposed financing deal with the London-based private equity firm. LIV Golf, which shook up professional golf after its launch in 2022, said on Thursday it would liquidate after losing key players and the funding needed to continue operating. BC Partners is seeking to acquire a $50 million bankruptcy loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the debtor-in-possession financing that would allow it to exert control over LIV Golf's Chapter 11 bankruptcy process, the FT report said, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report.

BC Partners declined to comment on the matter and LIV Golf could not be reached for a Reuters request for comment. FINANCIAL BACKING  BC Partners has told counterparties it still believes a global team-based golf group can succeed and remains willing to commit additional money and time to launching a LIV successor, according to the FT report. LIV filed for bankruptcy protection in September after the Public Investment Fund, which had invested more than $5 billion in the circuit since its launch, said it would end financial backing after the 2026 season. In April, the Saudi fund said LIV no longer fitted its investment strategy. The FT had reported on Wednesday that BC had abandoned a separate plan to relaunch LIV after failing to secure enough player commitments. Under that proposal, BC had lined up as much as $300 million in financing to stage tournaments in 2027, but the effort unravelled after a number of prominent players declined to commit to the league, the report said. The previous deal also collapsed after players made a series of demands that BC was unwilling to meet, the FT report added. The newspaper said between 15 and 40 players had expressed varying levels of interest, but some sought payment of financial guarantees that had been cancelled during the bankruptcy process and wanted the option to withdraw from the agreement even after signing commitments. Among the high-profile golfers to leave LIV since its bankruptcy filing was Jon Rahm, while Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed departed before the 2026 season.

Source: Reuters

TROMSO, Norway, Nov 8 : Several fans in the away section of Tromso's stadium fell through a hole in the stand and one person was taken to hospital during their Norwegian top-flight match with Bodo/Glimt on Sunday, both clubs said.  The game was stopped just before halftime when Bodo keeper Nikita Haikin called the referee's attention to the incident behind the goal where the away fans were standing in the pouring rain.  "We have had a serious incident in the away stand in connection with the game between TIL and Bodo/Glimt. Preliminary information is that a person has fallen through the stands, and is injured," Tromso said in a statement.  "Up to five people fell through the stands, and one was sent to hospital," Bodo press officer Simen Pedersen told Reuters in a text message.

Nov 8 : Two-time major winner Jon Rahm sealed a triumphant return to the DP World Tour on Sunday, winning the Abu Dhabi Championship a month after leaving LIV Golf. It was the former world number one's first tournament since he left the breakaway circuit, and the Spaniard hit a five-under 67 in Sunday's fourth round to finish 23-under, earning his 11th title on the DP World Tour. Tyrrell Hatton took second place, finishing two strokes behind Rahm, while Rory McIlroy was third. "It means a lot. Still almost not letting myself believe it. It's been quite a while since I've played good in a DP World Tour event," said Rahm, who had joined LIV Golf in 2023.

"In my last showing, if you don't count the withdrawals, I think I finished last. So, from last to first is a pretty good feeling." Rahm rose to the top of the leaderboard after the second round, sharing the position with Hatton and Francesco Laporta despite hitting three bogeys on the day. He claimed a solo lead on Saturday with an eagle and five birdies, finishing a stroke ahead of Laporta. The 31-year-old, who welcomed his fourth child with wife Kelley Cahill last month, shook off a bogey on the third hole to solidify his lead with six birdies in the final round. "After everything that's gone on and some poor play and some battles, mentally, with a lot of the noise, to come back out after a little bit of rest and having a new addition to the family, it's quite special," Rahm added. "I only wish they were here to celebrate with me."

Nov 8 : Anthropic has struck a deal worth about $3.4 billion to secure gas-fired power generators for data centers, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. The AI startup bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty generators in late September from OnePWR Solutions, a San Antonio, Texas-based equipment supplier, the report said. Strong demand for Anthropic's Claude family of AI models has prompted the company to secure additional computing and power capacity. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic expects to spend more than $500 billion over the next 10 years building AI infrastructure.
